races.name: Happy Retirement Martin Stoneman Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Martin Stonemans Lucky Last Handicap

runners_data.name: Two Plus Two
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two wins over 14f on Good ground and similar-going form reading 2W2P; Pat Cosgrave rides and Ed De Giles has a modest but live 1/5 14-day strike rate — this horse gets the race entirely on its terms and the style fit, though flagged at 0.93, is far less of a concern when it IS the only pace-setter in the field.

runners_data.name: Nymphaea
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani rides for J Candlish, who has been busy with 3 winners from 25 runs over 14 days; Nymphaea steps back up to 1m6f where she placed third at Southwell and ran second over 12f on Soft — she is a true hold-up type and will need Two Plus Two to come back to her, but she is probably the most capable of the closers if the pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Star Of Jupiter
runners_data.note: Has placed three times from five recent runs and run over this 1m6f trip on Standfast and Soft, showing she handles a stamina test; her natural preference is to come from off the pace, and though the runner data shows her mapped into midfield due to field congestion at the rear, she is a genuine hold-up horse who will be hunting down Two Plus Two from some way back — Harry Davies will need luck in running.

runners_data.name: Muhib
runners_data.note: Consistent handicapper who has placed in four of his last six starts including twice on Good ground over 12f; Warren Fentiman takes the ride for Olly Williams (0/2 over 14 days), and while the step up to 1m6f is untested for this horse — all recent runs are over 12f — the staying-on pattern in his form suggests the extra distance may not be unwelcome, though as a true hold-up type he remains structurally reliant on the pace collapsing.

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: The non-runner jockey flag is a notable negative and introduces real uncertainty about who rides; the seven-year-old has two wins at Nottingham in its record and the trainer B I Case has a 2/4 14-day strike rate, but recent form of 07-756 including a tenth and a seventh suggest this horse is well below its former level, and as a natural hold-up type it faces the same pace-chasing problem as its rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Two Plus Two is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine pace rival to push them, Pat Cosgrave can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits over this 1m6f trip on Good ground at Nottingham. The remaining four runners — Nymphaea, Star Of Jupiter, Muhib, and Regally Blonde — are all natural hold-up types, meaning they will be queuing up behind Two Plus Two with limited ability to disrupt the pace or force a tactical conversation. This creates a straightforward, controlled, single-pace race: a modest gallop from the front, minimal mid-race pressure, and a long straight run-in that could see the leader coast home before the hold-up horses can wind up their challenges. The race shape heavily favours a front-runner or prominent racer who can dictate and control; true hold-up profiles face the significant structural disadvantage of chasing a relaxed pace-setter with little cover from rivals to generate momentum.

scenarios.body: If Two Plus Two sets a stronger-than-expected gallop and flattens out in the final two furlongs, allowing the closers to pick up the pieces.

watchPoints.text: Two Plus Two's ability to control the gallop entirely unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if Cosgrave switches off and goes too slow, the closers will get a shorter race than expected and could close faster.
Regally Blonde's jockey is listed as NON-RUNNER, creating genuine uncertainty over who rides and whether any tactical instructions change — monitor the racecard for a late jockey booking.

Star Of Jupiter and Muhib are both true hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map — if they both attempt to race closer than their natural style, a bunched mid-race position could cause interference or traffic problems on the Nottingham straight.

Nymphaea was last seen just 17 days ago finishing second over 12f on Soft — the step back to 1m6f on Good is a different test, but her Southwell 3rd over 16f hints she may stay this longer trip better than her recent campaign over shorter suggests.

Good ground is confirmed across all Nottingham races today with no variation reported — no going concern applies to any runner, meaning the race is likely to be run at a true pace without the unpredictability of a testing surface to close the gap on Two Plus Two.

races.name: Cambion Electronics 65 Years In Manufacturing 'Hands And Heels' Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Rusheen Boy
runners_data.note: Won last time out and has a recent winning run over 7f on soft — stepping up to 1m½f on good ground is the key question, but as the lone front-runner he controls the tempo entirely, and his style fit score of 0.92 reflects that he may be stretched at this longer trip.

runners_data.name: My Boy Harry
runners_data.note: Boasts good form on good going with two wins at Goodwood and a recent third at Sandown; runs prominently in a blinkers-free style and this trip should suit well, making him a natural beneficiary of a steady Rusheen Boy-led gallop.

runners_data.name: Mariner
runners_data.note: Has found 8f on good ground within his comfort zone before, posting a second from a prominent position, and trainer Candlish has had one winner from 17 runs in the last 14 days — the tongue-tie and cheekpieces are noted but overall strike rate gives limited confidence.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: 90 days off the track is a concern, and his form string of 304666 on standard going shows a horse in a trough — a true hold-up type who needs the pace to truly collapse, which looks unlikely with a cluster of prominent horses in this field.

runners_data.name: Mbappe
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on standard going and has placed at this trip before, but the 141-day absence is a significant flag; Hope Regan claims 7lb which helps on the weights, and on a good surface he has the profile to finish powerfully if the pace plays into his hands.

runners_data.name: Volendam
runners_data.note: A genuinely prominent-natured horse who won over 8f on good ground and placed on soft — A W Carroll has had nine winners from 42 runners in the last 14 days, a strong yard, and Volendam is likely to push forward from his mapped midfield position into his natural berth near the pace.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Tom Easterby is firing with 10 winners from 103 over the past fortnight, and Perfidia's record on good going is excellent (12 of last 15 runs on similar ground with 2 wins and 8 places) — a natural front-rank performer squeezed onto paper midfield; expect Jake Dickson to push forward into a prominent position.

runners_data.name: River Wharfe
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has not won since scoring over 7f on standard going; a true hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping due to runner distribution, but with 58 days between runs and a form string ending in a zero, the route back to a clear finishing position looks difficult in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Rusheen Boy is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 1m½f Nottingham handicap and, with no genuine rival willing to press him from the gate, he is set to control proceedings at a comfortable, sustainable gallop on good ground. My Boy Harry and Mariner will look to sit close to the pace in a prominent position, likely tucked in just behind Rusheen Boy through the early stages, while the hold-up horses Bajan Bandit and Mbappe will settle towards the rear with a view to finishing strongly. This is a race shape that clearly favours horses capable of racing prominently or just off the pace — a measured, honest gallop that does not truly test stamina or generate a truly searching finish hands the rail-hugging stalkers a decisive advantage over those waiting for a late surge. The field holds more prominent types than the map can accommodate: Volendam and Perfidia are genuine front-rank horses displaced to midfield in this analysis because Rusheen Boy is firmly entrenched as the leader — in reality, both are likely to push forward and compete for the ground closest to Rusheen Boy, meaning the race will be run with a cluster of prominent types and not the tidy single-file shape the positions suggest.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Volendam and Perfidia push forward from their mapped midfield positions early — if both assert into the first two furlongs the pace could rise sharply and change the entire complexion of the race, testing Rusheen Boy's ability to control proceedings.

Mbappe's 141-day absence is significant — if he shows any ring-rustiness early under a 7lb claimer, his hold-up profile means he could find himself unable to land a blow from the rear even if the finishing straight opens up.

My Boy Harry's trainer J & S Best has only one winner from 11 runners in the last 14 days and the horse has not raced beyond 8f in form — jockey Kyle McHugh will need to place him perfectly to ensure the step up in distance does not expose a stamina limit.

Bajan Bandit returns after 90 days off and has shown a recent run of 666 finishes; monitor whether he can improve from the outside of the field or whether the hold-up position simply leaves him too much to do given the likely unhurried gallop.

races.name: Neigh More Early Starts For Martin Stoneman Handicap

runners_data.name: Return Of The Gods
runners_data.note: Trained by E Bethell and ridden by Pat Dobbs, this 3yo has a consistent run of 1-3-8 form at 6f on Standard (AW) but steps back onto turf today on Good ground, which is an unknown factor; natural prominent style suits the expected race shape and the 78-day break is worth monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Master Of Entropy
runners_data.note: Ran just 13 days ago and showed form at 8f on Good, but drops back to 6f here — a trip he hasn't proven on turf — and while his natural instinct is to race from off the pace, the compressed field means he's unlikely to get that clean run from the back as the map shows him occupying midfield rather than his ideal rear position.|

runners_data.name: Space Bear
runners_data.note: Listed as the confirmed pace-setter for this race but carries a NON-RUNNER tag, so the entire pace dynamic may shift materially if scratched; has 6f Good form (1W2P from 12 runs on similar going) and Mike Appleby's yard has hit form recently (T14: 2/14), making the NR status the single most important variable to verify before the off.|

runners_data.name: Cuban Lady
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's 4yo mare sports headgear (p) and has solid recent form over 6f on Good ground (1W2P from 9 similar-going runs); ridden by Marco Ghiani, she sits naturally prominent and her course form at this distance on Good makes her one of the better-placed runners if the pace is controlled — 34 days since last run is unremarkable.|

runners_data.name: Fenlander
runners_data.note: Won two of his last five starts, both over 6f on Good ground, and carries strong recent form (-23611); despite being shown in midfield on the map, he is a natural prominent racer whose recent winning profile means he will likely press forward regardless, and if he gets anywhere near his preferred berth he becomes a significant player in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Emperor Caradoc
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with headgear (p) and the best Good-ground record in the field (3W5P from 15 similar-going runs at this course and distance); a natural hold-up type whose patient style depends on something happening ahead of him, and his last four runs on similar going show a 1 and a 3 at 6f at Nottingham — legitimate closer threat if the gallop is genuine.|

runners_data.name: Paws For Thought
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran ridden by James Sullivan for D McCain Jnr, whose trainer has form (T14: 2/9), but carries a stamina flag — tagged as a horse that fades in the finish — and his recent form (109-07) on Good ground is inconsistent; naturally holds up but the fade tendency at the business end undermines confidence in any scenario where he needs to sustain a challenge.|

races.paceDynamic: Space Bear is the confirmed front runner here and, with no notable challenger looking to dispute the lead aggressively, should be able to control fractions from the gates on this straight 6f Nottingham track. Cuban Lady and Return Of The Gods will press forward into prominent positions, creating a competitive but measured gallop rather than a scorching pace collapse. This field contains more pace than the map can accommodate — Fenlander and Master Of Entropy are genuine prominent and hold-up types respectively but are shown in midfield positions because the race shape does not give them the room to secure their natural berths; of the two, Fenlander's recent 6f course form makes him the more likely to force his way into contention early, while Master Of Entropy will face a more constrained role than ideal. The resulting shape — a controlled, honest gallop with a settled front runner dictating — favours horses with genuine tactical speed who can sit just off the pace and pick up in the final two furlongs, meaning prominent-to-midfield closers with good form at this trip on Good ground carry the largest structural advantage.

watchPoints.text: Space Bear is marked as a NON-RUNNER — if confirmed scratched, the entire pace dynamic collapses and a contested or leaderless shape replaces the controlled scenario; check declarations.

Fenlander is a natural prominent type mapped to midfield due to field compression — if he pushes forward early as his profile suggests, the tempo rises significantly and that reorders which horses benefit.

Master Of Entropy drops from 8f back to 6f on turf for the first time in his recorded history shown here — the trip reduction is an unproven variable that could undermine his chance regardless of race shape.

Emperor Caradoc owns the strongest course record at this exact course and distance on Good going (3W5P from 15 runs) — worth tracking whether he gets a clear run late, as his hold-up style requires traffic-free passage in the final furlong on this straight track.

Paws For Thought's fade flag is particularly relevant over this 6f trip where the closing stages are unforgiving — monitor whether he weakens inside the final furlong as his recent form pattern suggests.

races.name: Martin Stonemans Final Furlong Handicap

runners_data.name: Invincible Crown
runners_data.note: Recent form shows 4th on Good ground at this trip, but the sim-going record reads a modest 0 wins 0 places from 6 comparable runs; a natural hold-up horse who will find herself further back than ideal in a field saturated with closers, making a clear run unlikely.|

runners_data.name: Comedian Leader
runners_data.note: 97 days off the track is a significant concern for a trainer with a modest 14-day strike rate of 0/4, and the horse's best sim-going figures came on Standard rather than Good; a genuine back-of-the-field operator whose true style is further compromised by the crowded hold-up group.|

runners_data.name: Doralee
runners_data.note: Trainer T D Barron fires in two winners from ten runners over 14 days, and Doralee's sim-going record on Good is comfortably the best of the hold-up horses at 1W3P from 12 comparable efforts; though her natural style places her at the rear, she has the most convincing form in this ground to suggest she can thread through if a gap appears.|

runners_data.name: Get Up Everybody
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a 3rd on Soft and a 3rd at 5f on Standard in recent starts, so the step back onto Good is not a red flag; jockey D Nolan knows the stable and the 27-day break should have freshened this one, though the 0W2P sim-going record suggests placing rather than winning form on this surface.|

runners_data.name: Sergeant Mayer
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — the hg:p headgear flag is noted and he carries 136lbs, but as the lone confirmed front-runner with no pace rival likely to take him on, he sets his own terms; STYLE_FIT tag at 0.93 means the race may not be run entirely in his comfort zone, but on a flat, straight track with an uncontested lead, he remains the key tactical influence throughout.|

runners_data.name: Irish Dancer
runners_data.note: Best form in this field on Good ground with a 2nd and a 1st from 8 comparable sim-going efforts, and the tb headgear suggests he travels positively; pressing Sergeant Mayer from a prominent pitch at 5f on this straight track puts him in the ideal position to pounce late, and trainer D Carroll has two winners from 19 runners in the last fortnight.|

runners_data.name: Beerwah
runners_data.note: Won at this course over 5f on Good ground (1/5f/GOO) and placed twice more at the same trip on Good — the most relevant course-and-distance form in this field; Marco Ghiani is an experienced operator and the b headgear means he should be switched on from the gate, placing him naturally in the prominent-to-midfield band that this race shape rewards.|

races.paceDynamic: Sergeant Mayer is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be allowed to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over this straight 5f at Nottingham. Irish Dancer will press from a prominent position and provide some company through the early stages, but neither horse is likely to set a truly punishing pace that tears the field apart. The result is a race likely run at an honest but not brutal tempo — enough to test stamina in the final furlong but not enough to dramatically compress the finish into a sprint from the rear. This shape strongly favours prominent or early-pressing types who can track the pace and pounce inside the final furlong, rather than genuine hold-up horses trying to make up ground from off it. This field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Invincible Crown, Comedian Leader, and Doralee are all genuine closers, but with three of them competing for the same territory, only one or two will find any daylight late, and the redistribution to midfield understates how far back they are likely to travel.

watchPoints.text: Irish Dancer's recent Good-ground course win and prominent running style make him the biggest threat to Sergeant Mayer — watch whether Zak Wheatley pushes him to press immediately or tracks half a length off through the first furlong, as that decision will shape the pace of the entire race.

Beerwah's course-and-distance winning form on Good ground is the standout piece of evidence in this field — watch how Marco Ghiani positions him out of the stalls, as a clean break and a prominent pitch could make him very difficult to pass in the straight.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Invincible Crown, Comedian Leader, Doralee) will all be hunting the same late ground — watch for traffic congestion in the final furlong if the pace does compress, as all three could block each other from getting a clear run simultaneously.

Sergeant Mayer's 38-day absence and 136lb weight are worth monitoring in the early exchanges — if he shows any sign of tiring earlier than expected before the 2f pole, the race shape changes immediately and prominent horses transitioning to hold-up tactics will benefit.
